features.how_it_works: _main is the verification workshop rather than shipped runtime: `_main/_audit-verify-all.cmd` runs the aggregated battery and records each step's rc, while `_main/battery-budget-oracle.py` enforces the per-step ratchet against `_main/battery-budget-baseline.json` and `_main/tooling-intent-oracle.py` checks that new instruments declare the bug they serve. `_main/yt-capture-replay-oracle.py` and `_main/yt-headless-paint-oracle.py` replay real player and paint fixtures offline, and `_main/dead-unwired-oracle.py` keeps the known-unwired twins from silently becoming second owners. Step timings live in `_cache/battery-steps.json`; none of this opens the owner's app.
inputs: Tracked source tree under `_main/`, `app/` and `worker/`
Battery step timings in `_cache/battery-steps.json` and `_main/battery-budget-baseline.json`
Oracle flags such as `--neg-arm` and `--record-step`
outputs: Per-oracle PASS/FAIL verdicts and rc on stdout
Step logs under `_main/_audit-verify/`
Ratchet updates in `_main/tooling-intent-baseline.json`
features.summary: _main is Sotto's verification workshop: the battery, oracles, fixtures and launch instruments that decide whether a change ships.

features.name: Recovered
features.how_it_works: `_recovered/worker_fab495ac.py` is the 4593-line snapshot recovered from the checkout that destroyed worker edits; `_recovered/worker_186c969e_HEAD.py` is the 4511-line pre-loss HEAD baseline kept so the diff is reproducible. Both are the same system-audio-in / JSONL-captions-out worker now maintained as `worker/sotto_worker.py`, and both are frozen: no shell imports or spawns them. `_main/RECOVERY.md` records the hash, size and what was deliberately not committed.
inputs: Frozen Python snapshots committed during the 2026-10-23 recovery
Diff receipts in `_main/RECOVERY.md` and `_main/INTEGRATION-11.md`
outputs: Reconstructable diff between pre-loss HEAD and recovered worker
No runtime JSONL and no app state
features.summary: _recovered holds frozen pre-loss copies of the ASR worker so the checkout that destroyed worker edits can be diffed and recovered.

features.name: Tools
features.how_it_works: All four files are read-only SQLite passes over the same agent runtime store: `_tools/cron-restore-probe.py` counts rows after the 13:11Z cutoff, `_tools/cron-restore-refute.py` moves the boundary onto the exact MAX row, `_tools/cron-silence-control.py` counts hourly session and message rows while that store was being written, and `_tools/cron-store-loose-ends.py` checks for another store and process lifetimes. They print POPULATION and WINDOW counts and never write or start an app. The verdict they support is kept in `_main/CRON-VERDICT.md`.
inputs: Read-only URI to C:/Users/Administrador/.minimax/v2/sqlite/runtime-state.sqlite
UTC cutoff and MAX timestamps from `_main/CRON-TRUTH.md`
outputs: POPULATION/WINDOW counts and pass-by-pass verdicts on stdout
Cron-silence evidence cited in `_main/CRON-VERDICT.md`
features.summary: _tools contains read-only SQLite probes that settled whether the agent's scheduled cron ever fired and recorded the verdict.

features.how_it_works: `app/_legacy-electron/main.js` is the retired Electron main process and says so explicitly: the live window is the pywebview shell in `app/webview/sotto_webview.py`. `preload.js` is the original `window.sotto` contract that the live shell ports line for line, and `worker-bridge.js` spawns the Python worker, parses its stdout as JSONL and feeds captions and statuses to the panel. `bridge-selftest.js` drives that real child-process pipe with hostile lines (a traceback, a non-zero exit, explicit flushes) and exits 3 when any step is not observed.
inputs: Child-process stdout JSONL (captions and statuses)
Renderer IPC messages such as hide, toggle, pointer and getInfo
outputs: Captions and statuses delivered to the panel receiver and main-process caption log
Bridge-selftest rc 0/3 with per-step receipts
features.summary: app/_legacy-electron preserves the retired Electron shell and preload bridge as the contract source for the live pywebview shell and as a testable worker-to-panel pipe.

features.name: Bend Core
features.how_it_works: `bend_core/LAWS.bend` holds the claims and model definitions, and `PROOF.bend` imports them with one proof per law for `bend PROOF.bend --verdict` in the `ubuntu-bend` WSL distro. `bend_core/model.py` is the same model written in Python for hosts without Bend 2: it checks named sample inputs and exposes `--selftest`, but is explicitly not the proof. The `NEGATIVE_*.bend` files are the red arms for laws that must fail.
inputs: Claims and model definitions in `LAWS.bend`
Witnesses in `PROOF.bend` and negative example laws
outputs: Lean verdict per law from the Bend gate
Python sample-check output from `model.py --selftest`
features.summary: bend_core states the Sotto caption and epoch laws in Bend/Lean with a Python model for machines without the Bend toolchain.

features.name: Discord
features.how_it_works: `discord/src/index.js` is the bot CLI: it takes `--guild` and `--channel`, reads `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and calls `capture()` in `discord/src/live.js`. `live.js` joins with `@discordjs/voice` and hands raw Opus packets to `receiver-core.js`, which maps SSRC to user and writes one continuous PCM file plus a packet JSONL per speaker with one decoder per stream. `discord/harness/two-speakers.js` drives the same core synthetically, and `worker/discord_streams.py` is the alternate reader reachable from `run.cmd --worker`, not from the live shell.
inputs: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN plus guild and voice-channel ids
Raw Opus packets tagged by SSRC from @discordjs/voice
outputs: 16 kHz mono PCM segments and packet JSONL under `out/<user_id>/`
Decoder-count and capture receipts
features.summary: discord is a bot-based capture tool that writes one continuous 16 kHz PCM stream per speaker for the worker to transcribe.

features.how_it_works: `probe/sotto_probe.py` is the two-question probe: it enumerates sounddevice inputs, captures a short loopback window and transcribes a synthetic WAV through faster_whisper, printing JSON and failing if either side has no evidence. `tap_probe.py` tests candidate tap devices for actual signal, `load_model.py` measures model load and device choice, and `laneshape.py`, `shape.py` and `native_imports.py` inspect agent-session lane shape and import availability. They are standalone instruments: no app module imports them.
inputs: Sounddevice device list and a 2 s capture window
Synthetic WAV for transcription
Agent session JSONL tree under C:/Users/Administrador/.minimax/v2/sessions
outputs: JSON evidence for loopback and ASR availability on stdout
Logs such as `probe/tap.log` and `probe/load.log`
features.summary: probe holds standalone measurements of this host's WASAPI loopback tap, ASR model load and session-lane shape.

features.name: Root Entrypoints
features.how_it_works: `_probe_schema.py` opens the minimax runtime-state SQLite read-only and prints schemas, a queue census and reference rows for queue, message and turn-ingress tables. `flicker-injection-harness.js` creates an Electron BrowserWindow and injects `_main/flicker-dom-oracle.js` through `executeJavaScript` to measure renderer flicker. Neither file is imported by the shipped shell; both are run directly from the repo root.
inputs: Read-only URI to C:/Users/Administrador/.minimax/v2/sqlite/runtime-state.sqlite
Electron runtime plus `_main/flicker-dom-oracle.js`
outputs: Schema and queue census on stdout
Flicker measurement results
features.summary: root-entrypoints are two root-level instruments: the runtime queue schema dumper and the Electron flicker-injection harness.

features.name: Tools
